summary: Thanks for the letter; I got a lot out of it. Before I plunge on to nice things I would like to respond to your indignation at my seeing some socially redemp­ tive elements in what you call “criminals,” which is to say the street kids of today who don’t hold with the idea that property is sacred. Among those I knew there was a wide-spread awareness, however, that life is sacred; none of these kids, whatever else they did, ever injured an animal, and often took great care for their welfare. It was as if by losing their sense of the sacredness of inert property they transferred more love to living things ... which is fine by me. That they would rip off or destroy a car or phonebooth or gum machine does not put them in a class with those who would torture animals, either in degree or kind. As to damaging art... well, many of them made ceramic objects and so forth, and thought more of the value of hand-produced unique artifacts than certainly do the rednecks down at the barber shop reading Playboy. Enough about that. Both the New Left, the hippie movement and the street drug subculture have more sense of the worth of art—and do more to produce it—than the guy watering his lawn in front of his tract house; what he’s worrying about is somebody scratching the paint job on his new Buick. That’s what he defends and treasures.
